BRICS, representative of Global South, is a real counterpoint to G7. Today BRICS nations are not just third world economies. BRICS is an existential collaboration because to grow in a sustainable manner we are already seeing a potentially catastrophic impact of climate change, and the people most affected are in the Global South.
  • BRICS can achieve practical South-to-South problem solving around food security, sustainability, climate resilience, affordable and inclusive innovation and employing young people in a productive way.
  • BRICS is a historic opportunity and its potential is hosted by India because India is truly at the epicentre of all these complex dynamics.
  • Trumpian impacts made it clearer to BRICS how important energy independence and security are and much important renewable energy is.
  • For instance, India, always dependent on the oil-rich Gulf. China, which has a lot of oil reserves, today, China's auto industry and battery sector are world leaders.

    • Other BRICS economies are similarly visionary:

  • Consider Brazil, an astonishing country, a bit like India - very large, democratic and diverse. They understood the importance of energy security, sustainability and now Brazil is a new pioneer of biofuels. They have large amounts of forest cover and agricultural products. A lot of that bio-waste is used for making biofuels.
  • Russia has plenty of fossil fuels and it doesn't look like it may transition to renewable any time soon but China, India, Brazil and South Africa - rising economies - are on their path - The Trumpian era is making it clear to these nations that they have to be self-sufficient in energy.
  • India must meet its development needs and the challenge of raising a very large number of people out of poverty or lower middle income status. So there is a continuing fossil fuel dependence alongside other issues like transitioning the jobs of people working in mining etc.
  • Currently, India is not more sustainable than China or the west and we are still dependent on coal.
  • In terms of South-South problem-solving and working environmental resilience, there could be a BRICS Climate and Resilience Fund now, a real platform with significant funding.

    • The recent catastrophic floods in Nepal - submerging entire valleys, displacing hundreds of thousands and wiping out decades of development gains in 72 hours - are a case study in precisely what happens when world's most vulnerable communities are left waiting for a multilateral system that moves at the speed of diplomatic courtesy.

  • The green jobs opportunity is where the BRICS climate hub agreed - morally compelling but economically irresistible. India alone has the potential to generate 35 million green jobs by 2047.
  • Brazil's bioeconomy could employ 20 million in sustainable agriculture, forest restoration and green manufacturing by 2035.
